tested_scope: One bounded official-GitHub historical-audit surface leaf: organization/enterprise audit-log documentation and audit-log streaming documentation as possible non-mutating reconstruction sources for immutable-release publish/delete/tag-reservation generations after repository/local newest-state loss.

public_sources.title: Reviewing the audit log for your organization - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
observed: Organization audit log lists events from the last 180 days.
REST audit-log access for an organization requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
REST audit log retains Git events for seven days; other audit-log events can be retained for up to seven months.
GraphQL audit-log responses can include data for only 90 to 120 days.

public_sources.title: Using the audit log API for your enterprise - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
observed: Enterprise audit-log API access is for enterprise owners and requires audit-log authorization.
The documented enterprise audit-log view lists activity within the last 180 days and Git events for seven days.

public_sources.title: Streaming the audit log for your enterprise - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
observed: Streaming sends audit data to an external data-management system from the time streaming is enabled onwards.
Paused streams buffer for a bounded period and can lose older continuity after longer pauses.
Delivery is at-least-once, so duplicates are possible.

required_negative_controls.finite_retention_window: FAIL_FOR_ACCEPTANCE: documented retained history is finite (180 days generally, seven days for Git events; GraphQL 90-120 days). It cannot by itself prove an unbounded monotonic retirement floor after arbitrary later resurrection.
required_negative_controls.repository_id_or_name_reuse: UNRESOLVED_BY_THIS_SURFACE: bounded docs reviewed here do not establish a permanent stateless mapping from a recreated repository name/current repository identity to every deleted predecessor's immutable-release reservations.
required_negative_controls.immutable_release_specific_event_fields: NOT_PROVEN: the bounded official docs reviewed establish audit-log categories/access/retention but do not establish a complete immutable-release publish/delete/tag-reservation event schema sufficient to reconstruct a monotonic generation floor.
required_negative_controls.org_enterprise_paid_entitlement: FAIL_FOR_ACCEPTANCE: organization audit-log API documentation states GitHub Enterprise Cloud is required; enterprise audit-log/streaming also presupposes enterprise ownership. This violates the leaf's no-paid-entitlement acceptance condition.
required_negative_controls.export_or_api_rate_limit_interruption: FAIL_CLOSED_REQUIRED: the audit-log API is rate limited; repository transport may checkpoint around rate limits but the accepted authority cannot depend on timely exhaustive polling.
required_negative_controls.deleted_org_or_repository_history: NOT_PROVEN: no bounded-source proof was found that current stateless access after deletion/recreation can enumerate every needed predecessor history for the required horizon.
required_negative_controls.unknown_prior_tag: FAIL_FOR_DISCOVERABILITY: finite/current audit-history queries do not establish a provider-enforced maximum immutable generation when the prior tag/digest is unknown and local newest-state is lost.
required_negative_controls.zero_finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota: FAIL_FOR_ACCEPTANCE due Enterprise Cloud entitlement requirement and finite retention semantics.
required_negative_controls.zero_incremental_cost: No incremental spend was incurred by this bounded documentation audit, but the candidate mechanism itself is not accepted because it requires enterprise entitlement and finite retained history.

observation_vs_inference.observation: Official GitHub documentation explicitly gives finite audit-log retention windows, enterprise access requirements for the organization audit-log API, and external-system dependence for audit-log streaming.
observation_vs_inference.inference: Therefore audit-log history cannot be the standalone zero-paid-entitlement, statelessly discoverable, provider-enforced monotonic retirement floor required by Part90. This is a scope-limited architectural falsification, not a claim that no undocumented/internal/future GitHub mechanism could exist.

result.new_falsification: Official GitHub audit-log/history surfaces are bounded by finite retention and/or Enterprise Cloud entitlement; streaming additionally depends on an external data-management sink and only begins from enablement. They do not satisfy the required stateless, indefinite, zero-paid-entitlement retirement-floor contract.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A provider-enforced historical authority surface that is statelessly discoverable from the current repository/incarnation, exposes a complete predecessor-generation lower bound across delete/recreate, survives arbitrary required horizon without external storage, and requires neither paid/finite entitlement nor mutative probing.

conflict_check: Single bounded Part91 leaf only; predecessor Part90 supplied the unresolved discoverability child. No other role, downstream, O-derived, shared-ledger, or legacy semantic input was read.

Required negatives: lost predecessor ID, name reuse, transfer/rename, restore-window expiry, private/deleted predecessor invisibility, paid/admin-only endpoint, rate-limit interruption, no mutative probe, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero incremental cost. Accept only if current non-mutating provider metadata yields an unforgeable monotonic incarnation lower bound that survives the required resurrection/rollback scope without external storage; otherwise persist the exact identity-history gap and choose the next provider-side authority leaf for the following invocation.
